title: Venture Capital Revealed: Behind the Schemes They Haven’t Told You
summary: Stu Ellman explains venture fund economics, concentrated winners, financing cycles and recapitalizations. Eisman draws out the distinction between unrealized marks and cash returns, and the risk of funding cash-burning companies with short runways. Ellman argues that large funds, AI and established managers are concentrating available capital. Later industry data support that concentration. Claims that markdowns require a new round are corrected by fair-value guidance and partly qualified within the conversation. Most forecasts and proposed AI or tokenization opportunities belong to Ellman, not Eisman.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Stu Ellman, co-founder of RRE Ventures. The guest supplies venture experience and forecasts. Eisman’s explicit agreement on Amazon, cash-runway risk and unrealized returns is retained; exploratory questions do not transfer other guest claims to him.
framework_points: Separate DPI and realized cash from paper IRR.
Test how entry prices change a successful company’s contribution to fund returns.
Consider financing reserves and contractual priority alongside business quality.
Distinguish illiquid valuation judgment from permission to ignore deterioration.
Use recent deployment to identify active venture investors.
tools_and_charts: Fund return multiples and carried interest
transcript_cautions: Full local MLX Whisper transcript read: 1,096 segments; no speaker diarization. Speaker attribution follows dialogue.
Several approximate historical prices and deal values are explicitly qualified by Ellman.
Bloomberg-era and Neuer Markt chronology are imprecise in the recollection; they are not treated as independent investment forecasts.
DPI is described colloquially in the dialogue; the analytical distinction is distributions versus paid-in capital, not the caption’s expansion.
The guest first overstates markdown freedom, then explicitly acknowledges accounting rules and audits.
